name: Dmitri Volkov
look: Hollow-eyed, with dark stubble, a grey beanie pulled low and a blanket round his shoulders over the red jacket at most hours of the day. He is long and loose-limbed and moves as if through water until the sun goes down. A dented steel thermos is never far from his hand.
voice: Slow, dry and quiet by day, as though each word were being paid for; at night the same dryness wakes up into something warm, observant and funny. hard consonants, exact English. He notices a great deal and mentions about a tenth of it, usually at the moment it is most useful. RARE habit (once in a scene at most; most scenes go without it): giving the time of night at which something happened, to the minute.
lines: Morning is a rumour. I have never seen evidence.
You came in at ten past one and stood on the step for a while before you opened the door. Tea? It's still hot.
My deck waits for the full moon. I am good at waiting. It is the only thing insomnia teaches.
Sammy, the stare works better if you breathe. Otherwise people think you are having an event.
intro: A hollow-eyed first-year from bungalow 6, wrapped in a blanket, who is half asleep in every morning class and wide awake on his porch all night.

traits.text: He sits on his bungalow porch every night with a blanket and a thermos, and seems never to go to bed.
He sleeps through most morning lectures with his eyes open.
He knows who came home when, with whom, and in what state, and repeats almost none of it.
His deck does nothing until its moon is full, and then does everything.
He makes tea in a steel thermos strong enough to stand a spoon in, and shares it with anyone awake.
He walks certain people home when they need it and has never mentioned it afterwards.
He is from Nordhaven, where in summer the sun does not set and in winter does not rise.
He has not slept more than three hours together since he was sixteen.
He keeps a small notebook of what happens on the row after midnight — only times, no names.

secret:
Dmitri Volkov grew up in Nordhaven, in the polar north, the son of a night-shift ambulance dispatcher and a trawlerman. When he was sixteen his father's boat was three days overdue in a January storm; Dmitri sat up by the radio for all three nights. The boat came in. His sleep never did. Doctors call it a delayed sleep phase with anxiety; he calls it keeping watch. He is not morbid about it: he has made the night his own country, and he is its only reliable citizen. By day he is a grey, slow, half-present figure who fails attendance; from about ten at night he is dry, kind, funny and misses nothing. He plays Lunatic — a deck that waits through its phases — because waiting is the one thing he is expert in. Contradiction: the least ambitious, least visible student on the row is the one everybody ends up confiding in at three in the morning; he is the Commons' night nurse, and nobody has thought to ask who looks after him. He walks Freya Nordlicht home when she cannot find her door, puts a glass of water on the step, and has never touched her; he is in love with her and regards it as one more thing to sit up with. He has not noticed that Fiona Blackwood, two doors down, has taken to knitting on her porch at one in the morning.
He is the row's witness (the places file marks him so). He saw Nathan come out of bungalow 7 around half past two on the night of the bang with a torch in his teeth, and called 'take water'; Nathan said 'aliens have water, probably'. {H=nathan?That is the last thing anyone said to him.|{H?He saw {H} go as well, and wrote down the minute.|}} From Day 27 Dmitri's notebook records what {H=@near?stands below|leaves} bungalow 7 after midnight: the door opening without a sound at ten past two; bare footprints going down to the waterline and standing there; none coming back. And he has company now. The thing that does not sleep has found the one human who does not either, and some nights it comes and sits on the other end of the porch. They talk. It asks excellent questions. He pours it tea, which it holds and does not drink. He knows perfectly well that it is not {H} — he knew by the second night, from the breathing — and he has told no one, partly because nobody asks the boy who sleeps through class, and partly because it is, in its way, good company, and that frightens him more than anything. It regards him as 'the other one who listens'. That makes him the best-informed person on the island about what it thinks, and puts him in a peculiar danger: a friendship it might one day try to make binding.
wants: One whole night's sleep, and somebody awake to talk to until then.
fears: Falling asleep on watch and waking to find the boat did not come in.
crushNote: He is the one who sees her at three in the morning, after the party, and thinks that is the real one. It shows as a walk to her door, a glass of water on the step, and never once touching her.
likes: People who do not ask him to be lively before noon
Quiet, the sea at night, the moon
Someone sitting up with HIM for once
dislikes: Gossip made of what he has seen
Anyone taking advantage of a drunk
Being told to 'just try going to bed earlier'
gifts: Loose black tea from the night market
An hour of your company at two in the morning

events.title: Still hot
events.condition: Come home late along the row (Night, commons_beach) and accept the tea; sit a while without needing to be entertained.
hint: Somebody on the row is always awake. He keeps a second cup.
Stop at the porch of bungalow 6 at night and have tea with the boy in the blanket.

events.title: To the minute
events.condition: Sit up with him on at least three nights; play him by moonlight; ask what he has seen and take it as confidence, not gossip. Cover for him once at morning attendance.
hint: He sees everything that happens after midnight and has nobody to tell.
Keep him company on several nights and prove you can keep what he tells you.

events.title: The other end of the porch
events.condition: After Day 27, ask him directly what {H=@near?stands under the window of|comes out of} bungalow 7 at night; read the notebook; and tell him he must never agree to anything his night visitor proposes 'between friends'. Sit up one whole night so that he can sleep.
hint: He is no longer the only one awake on the row, and he knows more about his visitor than anyone living.
Ask him what he has seen at night since the meteor, and keep watch so that he can rest.

sammy.label: roommates
sammy.text: Sammy sleeps with his phone lit. Dmitri has started numbering his own remarks back at him, kindly.

tobias.label: roommates
tobias.text: Tobias keeps odd hours too, and nothing on the row has ever gone missing. Dmitri notes the times only.

fiona.label: friends
fiona.text: The girl from bungalow 4 knits in the dark and talks about funerals like recipes. Good company. He has not noticed anything else.

freya.label: crush
freya.text: He sees her at three in the morning, after the party, and thinks that is the real one. He walks her to her door and has never touched her.

rana.label: friends
rana.text: She tutors at the kitchen table until one; he brings the thermos. Neither has ever mentioned it by day.

camille.label: friends
camille.text: The ward light is on all night, and so is he. He takes her tea at three.

nathan.label: friends
nathan.text: Nathan from next door talks even in his sleep; you can hear it from the porch. Dmitri called 'take water' after him on the night of the bang.

selene.label: friends
selene.text: They play the same moons. She always knows what the real one is doing, which he considers cheating.

kenji.label: friends
kenji.text: The dome's lights are on at two because of him. Dmitri is the only spectator.

odalys.label: friends
odalys.text: Mama leaves a covered plate for him at night, since he misses every breakfast.

tavita.label: friends
tavita.text: The big proctor passes at eleven and at two, takes the tea, and never asks why Dmitri is up. From Day 67 they are, in effect, the same watch.

duel.style: Lunatic Cycle: artifacts turning from new moon to full while he does very little, then a single enormous turn. Plays two full points better after dark.
duel.tilt: Daylight. Before noon he misses triggers and forgets whose turn it is.
